chunks: From him, from Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Azdi, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Should I name the Imams (peace be upon them) in the prayer? He said, 'Be general (do not name them specifically).'

key_terms.أَجْمِلْهُمْ: Be general with them, meaning do not specify their names individually
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةَ: The Imams, specifically referring to the Twelve Imams in Shia tradition
key_terms.فِي الصَّلَاةِ: In the prayer, referring to the ritual act of salat

ai.seo_question: Do I need to name the Imams when praying?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Aban ibn Uthman reports that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advised the narrator to 'be general' (*ajmil*) when mentioning the Imams during prayer, indicating that while specific naming is permissible, it is not obligatory and simplicity is preferred. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that *tawassul* through the Imams is recommended but not a pillar of the prayer, allowing for flexibility in liturgical expression. The instruction underscores the balance between reverence for the Ahl al-Bayt and the preservation of the prayer's structural integrity without unnecessary complication.
